nodes.name: Ni foam cleaning
nodes.procedure: A piece of Ni foam (2×5 cm) was cleaned by ultrasonication in 1M HCl, ethanol and deionized (DI) water (10 min for each), and dried.
nodes.source_text: A piece of Ni foam (2×5 cm) was cleaned by ultrasonication in 1M HCl, ethanol and deionized (DI) water (10 min for each), and dried.

nodes.name: NWOH hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: Precursor solution was prepared by dissolving 0.35 g of nickel nitrate and 0.30 g of ammonium paratungstate in 80 mL of DI water (Ni/W molar ratio = 9). The hydrothermal reaction was conducted at 180°C for 10 h in a Teflon-lined autoclave containing the precursor solution. Finally, NWOH obtained on Ni foam was rinsed with DI water and ethanol and then dried at 60°C for 12 h.

nodes.name: NWN nitridation
nodes.procedure: NWOH polyhedrons were further heated in a tube furnace at 500-650°C for 60 min under a flowing ammonia (200 sccm) and argon (50 sccm) gas mixture at a heating rate of 5°C/min; samples were then cooled naturally to room temperature under argon gas flow (250 sccm).

nodes.name: NFO dip coating
nodes.procedure: Precursor solution was prepared by dissolving nickel nitrate and iron nitrate (in equal molar concentrations of 0-0.03 g/mol) in 10 mL of dimethylformamide (DMF). NWN polyhedrons were soaked in the precursor solution for 15 min and exposed to an N2 gas stream to remove excess precursors; they were then dried at 80°C for 4 h.

nodes.name: RuO2 and Pt/C electrode preparation
nodes.procedure: Catalyst ink was prepared by mixing 10 mg of Pt/C or RuO2 powder and 10 μL of Nafion in 1 mL of a water/ethanol mixture (3:1). The catalyst powder was dispersed using ultra-sonication and uniformly coated on clean NF via drop casting. The prepared electrodes were heated at 60°C for 6-8 h.

nodes.name: NiO powder synthesis
nodes.procedure: Precursor solution was prepared by dissolving 0.35 g of nickel chloride and 0.53 g of urea in 80 mL of DI water. The hydrothermal reaction was conducted at 120°C for 8 h in a Teflon-lined autoclave containing the precursor solution. The obtained powder sample were rinsed with DI and then dried at 60°C for 12 h. The dried powder sample annealed at 350°C for 2 h in atmospheric condition.

nodes.characterization_summary: WN and NWN samples showed distinct peaks at 36.3, 46.5, and 64.4° corresponding to the (101), (105), and (110) lattice planes of W5N4 structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The WN and NWN samples showed distinct peaks at 36.3, 46.5, and 64.4°, corresponding to the (101), (105), and (110) lattice planes of W5N4 structure (JCPDS: 65-4761).

nodes.characterization_summary: Radial structure function around Ni shows dominant peak at 2.16Å corresponding to Ni-Ni coordination, indicating alloy formation in NWN sample.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The radial structure function around Ni was determined by the Fourier transform of EXAFS for NWN sample as shown in Fig. 1b. The dominant peak at 2.16Å corresponds to the Ni-Ni coordination.

nodes.characterization_summary: NWN shows Ni 2p peaks at 852.68 eV (Ni⁰, major) and 855.13 eV (Ni²+); W 4f shows W⁰ at 31.57 eV (emerges after Ni alloying) and mixed W⁴⁺ (33.06 eV), W⁵⁺ (33.83 eV), W⁶⁺ (35.36 eV); N 1s W-N binding energy shifts by 0.27 eV higher in NWN vs WN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high resolution X-ray photoelectron spectrum (XPS) of a NWN sample in the Ni 2p region exhibits a major peak at 852.68 eV, assigned to Ni⁰, and another peak at 855.13 eV for the Ni²⁺ state... High resolution XPS of the WN sample in the W 4f region showed mixed oxidation states of W⁴⁺, W⁵⁺, and W⁶⁺, with well-fitted fragment peaks at 33.06, 33.83, and 35.36 eV, respectively... The Ni-WN alloying procedure allowed for the emergence of a W⁰ peak at 31.57 eV in the NWN sample... From the N 1s spectra, W–N's binding energy in the NWN sample shifted by 0.27 eV compared to that of WN.

nodes.characterization_summary: NWN shows highly porous polyhedron surface; NWN/NFO shows thin NFO layer with no morphological differences from bare NWN.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HR-SEM images of the optimized NWN sample are shown in Fig. 2a and b. The ammonia treatment made the polyhedron surface highly porous.

nodes.characterization_summary: NWN shows metallic Ni d-spacing 0.20 nm (111) and W5N4 (101) 0.24 nm; NWN/NFO shows NiFe-LDH (003) 0.48 nm and γ-NiFeOOH (100) 0.25 nm after ECR.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high magnification image of a single polyhedron indicates metallic Ni with a d-spacing of 0.20 nm, corresponding to the (111) plane. Another high magnification image from the bulk polyhedron shows a lattice distance of 0.24 nm, corresponding to the (101) plane of W5N4.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform W distribution and slightly random Ni distribution in NWN polyhedrons; uniform Fe distribution at edges of NWN/NFO after ECR.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (STEM-EDS) images show uniform distribution of W elements in the W5N4 lattice and a slightly random distribution of Ni elements overall in the polyhedrons.

nodes.characterization_summary: Work functions: WN 5.59 eV, NWN 5.41 eV, NWN/NFO 5.54 eV, NFO 3.73 eV; both WN and NWN show metallic behavior.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The obtained W values of the WN, NWN, NWN/NFO, and NFO electrodes were 5.59, 5.41, 5.54, and 3.73 eV, respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: NWN polyhedron bulk shows distinct spots indicating high crystallinity; major planes (101), (110) indexed matching XRD analysis.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area diffraction pattern (SAED) image of the polyhedron bulk shows distinct spots, indicating the high crystallinity of NWN. The major planes identified from the XRD analysis, including the (101), and (110) planes, are indexed in the SAED pattern.
